paragraphs.text: [PDF page 1] Shahana Hanif 2025 Section 1: CAMPAIGN INFORMATION Candidate Full Name: Shahana Hanif Pronouns: she/her/hers Do you identify as a member of the LGBTQI Community? No NYC City Council District: 39 Full Name of Campaign Committee: Shahana Hanif 2025 Campaign Website: Shahanafrombk.com Campaign Social Media: X: @ShahanaFromBK; Instagram: ShahanaFromBK; BlueSky: @shahanafrombk.bsky.social; facebook.com/shahanafrombrooklyn If endorsed will you display the endorsement of the Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC in your literature whenever you list other endorsements, including on your campaign website? If no, please explain. Yes

[PDF page 2] Shahana Hanif 2025 Section 2: CANDIDATE EXPERIENCE & INFORMATION What experience do you have to demonstrate you are the best person to represent the office you are seeking? For the past eight years, I’ve worked in city government, first as Director of Organizing & Community Engagement in Council Member Brad Lander’s office, and now as the Council Member for District 39. I started out as a community organizer — working with public housing tenants, turning a vacant lot into the vibrant Avenue C Plaza, and supporting survivors of domestic violence. As a staffer in Councilmember Lander’s office, I resolved thousands of constituent cases and led initiatives like Participatory Budgeting, giving our community a direct voice in how millions of City dollars are spent. I also led organizing efforts, including ICE watches, Know Your Rights campaigns, and community education and mobilization efforts when Muslim and Jewish communities experienced hate. As a Council Member, I’m proud to have led the Council’s Progressive Caucus to push back against Eric Adams’ austerity budgets and his recent pro-Trump agenda. I wrote and passed the NYC Abortion Rights Act, Workers Bill of Rights, and Universal Curbside Composting legislation — while remaining rooted in our community and dedicated to serving the district that raised me. Since taking office in January 2022, my team and I have handled over 4,000 constituent requests, ranging from increased traffic enforcement to improved sanitation services. We’ve made significant strides in accessibility, including opening the elevators at the 7th Avenue F/G station, building a protected bike lane on 9th Street, and installing wheelchair-accessible swings at Van Voorhees Park. We’ve also expanded critical community services: our immigration legal clinic in Kensington now operates weekly, and our monthly food distribution has provided nearly 2,500 bags of food to working-class families in 2024. We also entered the top 10 City Council districts for new affordable housing, with the opening of 633 units and the Gowanus rezoning paving the way for thousands more. Additionally, I’m proud of my work to secure over $20 million in new funding for schools, parks, infrastructure, vital non-profits, affordable housing, and Participatory Budgeting projects. Please explain any activities and/or experiences that demonstrate your commitment to the LGBTQ+ movement, including any concrete achievements for the LGBTQ+ community that you are responsible for in your current, or previous, elected office/s or positions. Legislatively, I’ve sponsored and/or voted yes on Int. 976 to require accurate reporting on LGBTQIA+ youth in the shelter system, Int. 564 to establish citywide resource navigator for transgender, gender nonconforming, non-binary and intersex individuals as well as for cisgender women, and Int. 149 the Sex Worker Protection Act. In the citywide budget I’ve advocated for increased funding to important LGBTQIA+ initiatives such as the Lorena Borjas Transgender and Non-binary Wellness and Equity Fund, the LGBTQIA+ Inclusive Curriculum Initiative, Pride at Work, and the Trans Equity Initiative. As Co-Chair of the Council’s Task Force to Combat Hate, I have convened roundtables of students, including LGBTQIA+ students, to discuss how to combat hate and discrimination in schools. As a member of the Council’s Women’s Caucus, I voted in favor of Caucus bylaws to ensure that Caucus membership is open to future members of the Council who are trans women and that the scope of the Caucus’s work includes serving trans femme New Yorkers. When I was Council Immigration Chair, I opposed Mayor Adams’s appointment of Erick Salgado to a position in the Mayor’s Office of Immigrant Affairs due to his homophobic views. In my district, I’ve used discretionary funding to fund capital projects including gender-neutral school bathroom renovations and groups serving LGBTQ+ constituents including SAGE, Drag Queen Story Hour, VOCAL-NY and Girls for Gender Equity. Our office played a key role in supporting the designation of the Lesbian Herstory Archives building in the district as an official NYC Landmark. I’ve supported constituents in my district who’ve had appointments for gender-affirming healthcare cancelled by NYU Langone and Mount Sinai and called on all providers to continue providing care without discrimination.

[PDF page 3] I proudly march in the Brooklyn Pride Parade in my district every year! I was a vocal champion for Proposition 1, the New York Equal Rights Amendment, which passed last year. Please detail any specific policy proposals you may have that will affect the LGBTQ+ community. I am deeply proud to represent a vibrant LGBTQ+ community in my district. We are the proud home to Brooklyn Pride, the Lesbian Herstory Archives, and Ginger’s one of the few lesbian bars in New York City. Trump’s anti-queer and anti-trans agenda have already harmed many of my constituents. Right now, I’m working closely with LGBTQ+ advocacy organizations to amend and advance my bill, the Affirm Act (Int. 1201, previously identified as T2025-3093), which was heard by the Committee on Women & Gender Equity in February. This bill would update an existing local law on the prevention of interference with access to reproductive health care facilities, by prohibiting activities that prevent access to facilities offering gender-affirming care. This bill would also expand a person’s private right of action for interference with reproductive or endocrine medical care when a lawsuit is commenced against the person on the basis of this care, to explicitly include all forms of gender-affirming care. I’m grateful to the guidance that many LGBTQ+ groups are currently providing me to ensure the bill text reflects my legislative intent. I also joined my colleagues in introducing a suite of legislation to protect trans New Yorkers which are detailed here: https://gaycitynews.com/city-lawmakers-council-tgncnbi-new-yorkers-trans/ I am also fully supportive of the Pride in Policy report that my colleagues in the Council’s LGTBQ caucus authored with the support of LGBTQ+ issue experts- https://drive.google.com/file/d/1F6jbkJJk5gKpjqowAYFnpLfJ585Mv7u3/view?fbclid=PAZXh0bgNhZW0CMTEAAablFhn4MvL TXjt3QzaVc2ZV4eF156Yj7eBPWea43nrNuqw8VhUTDoOc2Gw aem _ _ HqYwCTtBOCrGPihareChYQ Please list here the union, organizations (community, civic, media, issue groups), LGBTQ+ leaders, and elected officials that have endorsed you. I’ve been endorsed by the following organizations: 1199, SEIU, 32BJ, Bangladeshi Americans for Political Progress, BK Forge, Brooklyn Young Democrats, Citizen Action, Churches United for Fair Housing, DRUM Beats, Indivisible Brooklyn, the Jewish Vote, Lambda Independent Democrats of Brooklyn, Muslim Democratic Club of NYC, New Kings Democrats, New Majority NYC, New York Progressive Action Network, Planned Parenthood of Greater New York, PSC CUNY, Up Next NY, and the Working Families Party. I’ve been endorsed by the following elected Officials: Public Advocate Jumaane Williams, Brooklyn Borough President Antonio Reynoso, Former Manhattan Borough President Ruth Messenger, State Senator Andrew Gounardes, Council Member Tiffany Cabán, Council Member Crystal Hudson, Council Member Rita Joseph, Council Member Chi Osse, Council Member Sandy Nurse, Council Member Lincoln Restler, District Leader Lydia Green, District Leader Aaron Ouyang, District Leader Jacqui Painter, and District Leader Julio Peña. Have you ever endorsed any LGBTQ+ candidates? Which ones? Yes. I’ve endorsed Council Member Tiffany Cabán, Council Member Crystal Hudson, Council Member Chi Ossé, State Senator Jabari Brisport, District Leader Lydia Green, Ana Maria Archila for Lieutenant Governor, and Yuh-Line Niou for Congress.

[PDF page 4] Shahana Hanif 2025 Section 3: VISION FOR LEADERSHIP Across the nation, and here in NY, we have seen a massive wave of anti LGBTQ+ legislation, particularly targeting the transgender community. If elected, how will you use your platform to protect LGBTQ+ people? What is the role of the office you are seeking in combating these attacks on our community? I am laser focused on making sure my LGTBQ+ constituents are championed by their Council Member both in the District and in City Hall. I’ve been attending/sponsoring events like Parents of Gender Expansive Kids’ Gender Expansive Families Propaganda Party, Drag Queen Story Hour, and The Center’s Community LGBTQ+ Iftar to make sure I’m using my platform to uplift my queer siblings. In Council Chambers, I’m working to pass the trans rights package I’ve previously referenced as well as the Pride in Policy suite of bills. We have seen significant hate crimes and targeted attacks against LGBTQ+ New Yorkers in recent years. What is the role of the office you are seeking in responding to these acts and how can we work to reduce discrimination in our City? As Co-Chair of the Council’s Task Force to Combat Hate, I am currently working on white paper that will include recommendations including: -Fully funding the Office for the Prevention of Hate Crimes and community groups like the Anti-Violence Project that specialize in LGBTQ+ self-defense, bystander training, and education. -Improving diversity in our curriculums so all students learn about how LGBTQ+ history and culture have shaped New York City. -Strengthening legal protections of patients accessing gender-affirming healthcare. -Increasing survivor services for victims of hate violence. -A full investment in the Mental Health programs laid out in the Progressive Caucus’s Crisis to Care Plan: https://nycprogressives.com/crisis-to-care/ The NYPD has historically targeted LGBTQ+ community members for arrest or harassment, violating constitutionally protected rights and abusing their discretionary powers in discriminatory ways. Although great efforts have been made by LGBTQ+ community leaders to improve the NYPD Patrol Guide to inform interactions with LGBTQ+ New Yorkers, we continue to see that those guidelines are not being followed. How will you ensure that local law enforcement officials engage appropriately with LGBTQ+ New Yorkers, specifically trans women, and that there is appropriate oversight of the NYPD? In my time in the Council, I’ve consistently pushed for systemic reform to the NYPD and will continue to do so. I support the following policies: -The removal of the VICE and SRG units, whose unchecked violence has particularly harmed LGBTQ+ New Yorkers. -Reforms to protest policing, including but not limited to implementation of the agreement secured by Attorney General James following the police violence that occurred during 2020 racial justice protests. -The full implementation of the How Many Stops, Right to Know, and Community Safety Acts. -An end to biased and harmful Stop-and-Frisk and broken windows policing tactics. -Establishing a citywide response system for mental health crises that uses health-focused and peer-led best practices instead of defaulting to violent police tactics. Genuine accountability for police misconduct. Sex workers are part of our community. Do you agree to uphold the rights of sex workers and support the Sex Worker Protection Act? Would you support the removal of the VICE Squad, which has been found to be violent towards people in the sex trade? Yes, I am a proud sponsor of the Int. 149, the Sex Worker Protection Act. I am working to get this bill heard and passed in my capacity as Progressive Caucus co-chair. https://legistar.council.nyc.gov/LegislationDetail.aspx?ID=6557435&GUID=975B28C0-94B0-4E99-97B1-E9CE32531C88&O ptions=&Search= Yes, I strongly support disbanding the VICE Squad. I highlighted this policy priority in my joint report with Comptroller Lander and Council Member Cabán “The Path Forward to a Feminist Recovery” https://comptroller.nyc.gov/reports/the-path-forward-to-a-feminist-recovery/ (see Recommendation 9, which is excerpted below)

[PDF page 5] "NYPD’s Vice Enforcement Division (Vice), which is responsible for cracking down on consensual sex work, should be disbanded immediately. Vice has consistently demonstrated that it is a rogue unit within an already unaccountable department that cannot be trusted to operate in the city. One of their common practices is to disguise undercover officers as buyers of sex, encourage someone into verbally agreeing to exchange sex for money, and subsequently make an arrest. Even at its most routine, this is a coercive tactic that punishes consensual sex workers for participating in arrangements that should be decriminalized. At its most egregious, officers have repeatedly used this arrangement as a vehicle for systematic sexual harassment and assault. In both cases, the workers that are harmed are predominantly women and gender non-conforming people who are Black and Brown, immigrants, and/or LGBTQ+ . Instead of arresting these New Yorkers, the City should be supporting them with economic empowerment tools and connections to housing, health care, and other essential services. " Many in our community are refugees and undocumented immigrants. Do you support NYC remaining a sanctuary city and barring city agencies like NYPD from cooperating with ICE? Yes

[PDF page 6] Shahana Hanif 2025 Section 4: RELEVANT POLICY POSITIONS Trans Equity Do you support trans kids playing on sports teams in accordance with their gender identity, in accordance with DOE policy, New York City and State Human Rights Laws, and the NYS Constitution? Why, or why not? Yes Do you support ensuring all individuals, including trans New Yorkers of all ages are able to access medically appropriate health care services, including reproductive health care and gender affirming care regardless of their gender identity? Why, or why not? Yes Funding Do you support continuing and sustaining funding of the Trans Equity Initiative, which provides funding to several community-based organizations for programming provided specifically to transgender, gender non-conforming and non-binary New Yorkers? If no, please explain. Yes Nonprofit organizations play a vital role for LGBTQ+ New Yorkers, serving as trusted community partners for addressing homelessness, hunger, healthcare, education, and more. However, chronic delays in city payments have left many organizations on the brink of collapse, threatening the services LGBTQ+ residents rely on every day. Do you commit to reforms that streamline the bureaucratic process, prioritize timely payments, and support financial stability for nonprofits serving the LGBTQ+ population? If no, please explain. Yes Health Care Will you support increased funding for the NYC Council Ending the Epidemic Initiative and the HIV/AIDS Services Administration? If no, please explain Yes Will you support fully funding NYC Department of Health’s plan to expand PEP & PreP Access? If no, please explain. Yes Housing The LGBTQ+ community is in great need of senior housing for many of our aging population. Would you help with the funding and siting of senior housing for the LGBTQ+ community in your district and across the city? If no, please explain. Yes Will you support increasing funding for both emergency shelter beds and transitional beds for homeless youth, a large percentage of whom are from the LGBTQ+ community? If no, please explain. Yes Law Enforcement Enforcement agencies, such as the NYPD, DOHMH, and DEP, often target LGBTQ+ businesses for aggressive and discriminatory enforcement actions, particularly as part of Multi-Agency Responses to Community Hotspots (MARCH) raids. Do you support changing the way enforcement actions take place to ensure the LGBTQ+ businesses are treated equally by agencies? If no, please explain. Yes The plan to close Rikers and replace it with borough jails is still on the books, but little progress has been made. At the same time, conditions at Rikers have continued to deteriorate, including the collapse of trans affirming units and policies critical to the safety, dignity, and fair treatment of LGBTQ+ people at Rikers. What should be done now to address the issues on Rikers? What is the role of the office you are seeking in moving forward? I will continue urging the Mayor to follow the City’s legal mandate to close the jail facilities on Rikers Island by 2027. While the facilities remain open, I support appointing an independent federal receiver to take over operations and taking steps to improve immediate conditions including, but not limited to:

[PDF page 7] -Reducing the jail population via faster processing times, expansions of proven alternative to incarceration programs, and initiatives that reduce recidivism including supportive housing. -The full implementation of the ban on solitary confinement -Improving access to narcan to address overdose issues through my bill Intro. 206 -Better addressing the health needs of detained people, especially those who are trans or gender non-conforming -Closing the Rose M. Singer center.
